claims.text: A combinatorial design-of-experiments approach can be used to study the effects of changing individual elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Changing individual elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr HEA will produce systematic changes in its mechanical properties.
The anticipated mechanical-property changes arise from modified lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr HEA has a near-equiatomic composition.
Controlled synthesis ensures a homogeneous microstructure in the initial alloy.
Varying constituent concentrations changes local lattice distortion.
Varying constituent concentrations changes the distribution of atomic-size-induced stress fields.
Local lattice distortions and atomic-size-induced stress fields govern solid-solution strengthening and phase stability.
Altered elemental percentages modify the alloy's chemical complexity.
Changes in lattice distortion and chemical complexity affect dislocation motion.
Changes in dislocation motion alter mechanical strength and ductility.
Yield strength, tensile strength, and ductility will correlate systematically with specific elemental-composition changes.
Maintaining identical processing conditions isolates compositional effects from processing-induced effects.
The effect of each element may be nonlinear because of interactions among multiple constituents.
